# XSLT Playground

> XSLT Playground (xsltplayground.com) is a free online XSLT editor and tester. It runs XSLT 1.0, 2.0 and 3.0 on real server-side processors (XSLTC for 1.0, Saxon 9 for 2.0, Saxon HE 12.9 for 3.0), so results match what those processors do in production. No installation or sign-up.

## Tools

- [XSLT Playground](https://xsltplayground.com/): the editor. Stylesheet, XML input, named parameters and result side by side; XSLT 1.0, 2.0 or 3.0.
- [XSLT 2.0 tester](https://xsltplayground.com/xslt-2-0/): run stylesheets on Saxon in XSLT 2.0 mode.
- [XSLT 3.0 tester](https://xsltplayground.com/xslt-3-0/): run stylesheets on Saxon HE 12.9, including maps, arrays and JSON functions.
- [XPath tester](https://xsltplayground.com/xpath-tester/): evaluate XPath expressions against an XML document.
- [XML to JSON](https://xsltplayground.com/xml-to-json/): convert XML to JSON with XSLT 3.0.

## What it does

- Multiple XML inputs and parameters per transformation
- Trace of variables and a count of how often each construct ran, to see what a stylesheet actually did
- Errors reported with their code and line; clicking one jumps to that line
- Saved transformations with a short shareable link
- Up to 3 independent workspaces, exportable as JSON

## Reference

- [XSLT and XPath function reference](https://xsltplayground.com/blog/xslt/functions/): 229+ functions, each with an example you can run.
- [XSLT and Saxon error reference](https://xsltplayground.com/blog/xslt/errors/): common error codes explained, with fixes.
- [XSLT after Chrome removes it](https://xsltplayground.com/blog/chrome-xslt/): what stops working in Chrome 158 (17 November 2026) and how to migrate.

## Custom extension functions

The 2.0 and 3.0 processors expose extension functions under `xmlns:tib="http://www.tibco.com/bw/xslt/custom-functions"`, for stylesheets written for TIBCO BusinessWorks: about 50 of them, among them `tib:uuid`, `tib:timestamp`, `tib:add-to-date`, `tib:parse-date-time`, `tib:string-to-base64`, `tib:base64-to-string`, `tib:pad` and `tib:substring-after-last`. Each is registered under both its kebab-case and camelCase name.
